A scene from a warm, old-fashioned television space adventure: adult actors on a practical starship bridge set, played with complete sincerity.

On the large wall viewscreen, the Reptile Commander addresses the adult Captain, who sits in his command chair in the foreground with his back to the camera. The Reptile Commander holds his gaze out of the screen, tilts his scaled head a few degrees and speaks one line slowly, with cold calm certainty; his mouth and jaw move with the words and his amber eyes stay fixed. The Reptile Commander says: "You will surrender, or be destroyed." Then he closes his mouth and waits, unblinking.

The Captain does not move or speak; he listens, still, his hand resting on the armrest. The camera is locked off. The picture on the screen stays inside its frame.

REPTILE COMMANDER VOICE: A controlled, androgynous low-mid voice with smooth legato phrasing, neutral international English and very precise diction, shaped into an imperious antagonist by a restrained gravelly throat resonance and a short metallic communications reverb. Menacing through calm certainty, never screaming or a deep monster roar. Beneath the rasp is the same warm, composed intelligence as the Ship. Preserve this pitch, accent, smooth underlying cadence and light processing throughout the line.

Only the Reptile Commander speaks. Sound: the spoken dialogue exactly as written, the low hum of the bridge and soft console tones. No music, no narration, no other voices, no added lines. No subtitles, captions or on-screen text.
